text: Ahead scheduled event — referendum, election, central-bank decision — markets learn. event clock measures much outcome-relevant information arrived : event-clock time ,TA_{t,T} quadratic variation log-odds Lt=logit(qt)L_t = \mathrm{logit}(q_t) traded event probability qtq_t, ̂t,T=∑ti∈[t,T)[logit(qti+1)−logit(qti)]2.\widehat A_{t,T} \;=\; \sum_{t_i \[t,T)}   \bigl[\mathrm{logit}(q_{t_{+1}}) - \mathrm{logit}(q_{t_i})\bigr]^2 . quadratic variation ignores drift invariant equivalent measure changes, ̂\widehat needs assumption risk premia, constant level distortion qq (discounting, constant state-price tilt) drops . concept, identification results, empirical applications reproduced developed Hanke, Schadner, Stöckl, Weissensteiner (Working Paper), Learning Scheduled Events: Prediction Markets, State Prices, Option Valuation.

title: Measuring the event clock: Brexit, the 2016 U.S. election, and Polymarket
text: working paper evaluates clock one-month valuation date (May 24 / October 10, 2016) one-week, two-week, one-month horizons, battery robustness variants: reproduces published table: Brexit ̂\widehat 0.064 (1W), 0.166 (2W), 0.511 (1M) bipower 0.375; U.S. election 0.015, 0.046, 0.370 bipower 0.386 truncated 0.259. Two details worth noting: Truncation vs. largest-move exclusion. truncation rule (drop increments beyond 3 robust standard deviations) binds U.S. window — removes exactly largest move matches published 0.259 — Brexit window, whose largest move stays inside threshold. published Brexit “truncated” value (0.426) corresponds largest1. daily data short windows, always compare columns. Windows anchored, trailing. “1M” runs valuation date event date; observations calendar-daily including weekends.
code: gb <- event_clock(ep_gb,   from = as.Date("2016-05-24"),   to = c(`1W` = as.Date("2016-05-31"), `2W` = as.Date("2016-06-07"),          `1M` = as.Date("2016-06-23")) ) us <- event_clock(ep_us,   from = as.Date("2016-10-10"),   to = c(`1W` = as.Date("2016-10-17"), `2W` = as.Date("2016-10-24"),          `1M` = as.Date("2016-11-08")) )  tab <- rbind(   cbind(case = "Brexit", as.data.frame(gb[, c("horizon", "method", "A")])),   cbind(case = "U.S. election", as.data.frame(us[, c("horizon", "method", "A")])) ) knitr::kable(   stats::reshape(tab,     idvar = c("case", "horizon"), timevar = "method", direction = "wide"   ),   digits = 3,   col.names = c("Case", "Horizon", "RV", "Truncated", "Bipower",                 "Largest-1", "Largest-2") )

what: The event clock on live Polymarket data
title: Measuring the event clock: Brexit, the 2016 U.S. election, and Polymarket
text: package connects public, keyless Polymarket APIs. shipped polymarket2024 dataset downloaded exactly code:   jumps 2024 clock, matched ranking daily contributions (dL Trump-Yes log-odds): Jun 27–28 — Biden–Trump TV debate: largest hourly move whole sample (dL = +0.35), debate still air. Jul 13–14 — assassination attempt: largest tick overall (dL = +0.42) — 22% entire five-month clock one day. Jul 17–21 — Biden’s withdrawal: mostly priced July 17 reports; announcement modest tick. Aug 1–10 — Harris secures nomination, picks Walz, surges (dL = -0.20 -0.14). early–mid Oct — October rally (dL +0.11 +0.16 Oct 7/15/22), sharp intraday reversal Oct 23. Nov 2–3 — Selzer Iowa poll shock (dL = -0.17), reversed next day; election night. Conspicuously absent: September 10 Harris–Trump debate rank among top ticks — market priced barely informative, exactly long September plateau clock shows. intraday data, mind sampling frequency: microstructure noise (bid-ask bounce coarse tick grid) inflates measured variation. Collapsing one daily snapshot (last price 16:00 New York time) robust default:
code: # 1. find the event and the "Yes" token pm_search("presidential election winner 2024") mkts <- pm_markets("presidential-election-winner-2024") tok <- mkts$token_id[grepl("Trump", mkts$question) & mkts$outcome == "Yes"]  # 2. pull the hourly price history (chunked automatically) ep24 <- pm_prices(tok, from = "2024-06-01", to = "2024-11-06",                   market_id = "Polymarket: Trump wins 2024",                   event_date = as.POSIXct("2024-11-05", tz = "UTC")) data(polymarket2024) ep24 <- as_event_prices(polymarket2024,   market_id = "Polymarket: Trump wins 2024",   event_date = as.POSIXct("2024-11-05", tz = "UTC") )  events_24 <- data.frame(   date = as.POSIXct(c(     "2024-06-28 02:00", "2024-07-13 23:00", "2024-07-21 12:00",     "2024-08-03 12:00", "2024-10-15 12:00", "2024-11-03 00:00"   ), tz = "UTC"),   label = c(     "TV debate", "assassination attempt", "Biden withdraws",     "Harris surge", "October rally", "Selzer poll"   ) )  mark_events(plot_q(ep24), events_24) mark_events(plot_clock(event_clock_path(ep24)), events_24) c(   hourly = event_clock(ep24, methods = "rv")$A,   daily  = event_clock(pm_daily(ep24), methods = "rv")$A ) #>    hourly     daily  #> 1.2631246 0.7756132

text: as_event_prices() — standardize probability series (prediction markets, betting quotes, state prices) flag-don’t-drop cleaning; q_from_price() handles discount overround normalization. event_clock() — realized-variation estimator AA truncation, bipower, largest-move robustness variants; event_clock_path() cumulative clock time; event_clock_forecast() trailing-window real-time benchmark. Formula book — closed-form calculators (q,)(q, ): ec_moments(), ec_exceedance(), ec_revision(), ec_atm_event_call(), ec_sigma_eff(), ec_variance_share(), ec_iv_rule(), ec_target_clock(); exact transition law simulators (ec_transition_density(), ec_simulate(), ec_simulate_path()). Polymarket connector — pm_search(), pm_markets(), pm_prices(), pm_daily() public, keyless Gamma/CLOB APIs. Datasets — brexit2016, us2016 (working paper’s event windows), polymarket2024 (hourly 2024 U.S. election prices). Plots — plot_q(), plot_clock(), plot_clock_vs_calendar().

what: Convert traded state prices into risk-adjusted event probabilities — q_from_price
title: Convert traded state prices into risk-adjusted event probabilities — q_from_price
text: Traded event claims (prediction-market contracts, betting quotes, binary options) pay one unit resolution. price therefore discounted probability: \(\psi_t = D(t,\tau)\, q_t\), \(D(t,\tau)\) discount factor payout numeraire. function undoes discounting, alternatively removes bookmaker overround normalizing sum outcome prices book.

title: Convert traded state prices into risk-adjusted event probabilities — q_from_price
code: q_from_price(   price,   discount = 1,   book = NULL,   method = c("discount", "overround") )

title: Convert traded state prices into risk-adjusted event probabilities — q_from_price
text: price Numeric vector raw claim prices \(\psi_t\) (0-1 scale; rescale percent quotes first). discount Numeric scalar vector, discount factor \(D(t,\tau) \(0, 1]\) applicable payout (default 1, .e. discounting). book Numeric scalar vector, sum prices outcomes market. Required method = "overround". method Character, "discount" "overround".

title: Convert traded state prices into risk-adjusted event probabilities — q_from_price
text: numeric vector probabilities q. Values outside \([0,1]\) trigger warning (indicate wrong discount/book), returned unchanged caller can flag rather drop .

title: Convert traded state prices into risk-adjusted event probabilities — q_from_price
text: Two normalizations available: method = "discount" (default): \(q = \psi / D\). deterministic interest rates result risk-adjusted (risk-neutral) event probability; stochastic rates forward-measure probability. short horizons correction basis points systematic. method = "overround": \(q_j = \psi_j / \sum_i \psi_i\), book supplies \(\sum_i \psi_i\). Use raw quotes include bookmaker margin already removed data provider. Note series already margin-adjusted must normalized twice. level distortion (approximately) constant log-odds scale — constant discount factor, constant state-price tilt — shifts \(L_t = \mathrm{logit}(q_t)\) constant therefore leaves event clock unchanged: quadratic variation invariant level shifts. Getting level q exactly right matters probability statements, event_clock().

title: Convert traded state prices into risk-adjusted event probabilities — q_from_price
code: # a 90-day claim priced at 0.19 with a 2% (annualized) short rate q_from_price(0.19, discount = exp(-0.02 * 90 / 365)) #> [1] 0.1909393  # two-sided book with overround: prices sum to 1.04 q_from_price(0.52, book = 0.52 + 0.52, method = "overround") #> [1] 0.5
